regime_classification.growth: {"dimension":"growth","metric_summary":"GDP 7.8% YoY; PMI 56.5","signal_text":"GDP at 7.8% YoY and PMI Composite at 56.5 look unambiguous — until you notice that core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, and the GST surge to ₹2,31,290 cr / month is partly a services-economy story, not broad goods demand. The inversion: capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity is above the 75% threshold that historically triggers fresh private capex, which is genuinely encouraging — but if that capex is being funded by credit growing at 19.54% YoY against deposits at 16.86% YoY, the fuel tank is thinning. Quality of growth is good at the top; the plumbing underneath is under stress.","badge_label":"Expansion Mode","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.inflation: {"dimension":"inflation","metric_summary":"CPI 6.09% YoY; Fuel 22.93% YoY","signal_text":"Headline CPI at 6.09% YoY is above the RBI's 6% tolerance ceiling, but the decomposition is what matters: food at 8.94% YoY is doing most of the damage, while core CPI at 4.5% YoY — though rising — is not yet a structural emergency. The dangerous signal is fuel at 22.93% YoY, at the 95th percentile of its 10-year range, feeding directly into WPI at 9.92% YoY. The second-order effect: fuel inflation compresses margins for transport-intensive sectors, feeds into food prices with a one-quarter lag, and makes the RBI's extended pause increasingly difficult to defend publicly.","badge_label":"Inflation Overshoot","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.credit: {"dimension":"credit","metric_summary":"Credit 19.54% YoY; CD ratio 82%","signal_text":"Bank credit at 19.54% YoY — rising for three consecutive months — against deposit growth at 16.86% YoY is a 268 bps divergence that has widened every month this cycle. The CD ratio at 82% is at the 75th percentile of its 10-year range; the last time it sustained above 80% during a rate-pause cycle, macro-prudential tightening via risk weights followed within two quarters. NBFC credit growth decelerating to 15.4% YoY from 15.8% signals wholesale funding stress is already biting at the margin; corporate bond issuance at ₹1,34,000 cr / month confirms firms are routing around the banking system.","badge_label":"Deposit Gap Stress","badge_type":"b-risk"}
regime_classification.policy: {"dimension":"policy","metric_summary":"Repo 5.25% p.a.","signal_text":"Repo at 5.25% p.a. is unchanged, but the real rate is being compressed by the day: with headline CPI at 6.09% YoY, the real repo rate is negative. The RBI's own inflation forecast of 5.1% YoY is already stale — fuel at 22.93% YoY and food at 8.94% YoY make that forecast a rounding error. The practical consequence: a rate cut is off the table, a hike is politically difficult, and the pause is becoming a slow-motion tightening via rising deposit rates as banks compete for funds — NIM compression is the transmission mechanism the policy communiqué won't mention.","badge_label":"Rate Pause","badge_type":"b-neu"}
regime_classification.capex: {"dimension":"capex","metric_summary":"IIP CapG 16.9% YoY; CU 77.4% of capacity","signal_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY — the third consecutive month of acceleration — combined with capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity crossing the 75% threshold is the most credible private capex signal in two years. Steel output at 8.2% YoY and cement at 6.1% YoY confirm this is physical investment, not statistical noise. The inversion: if credit funding this capex is sourced from a banking system running a CD ratio of 82%, and wholesale funding costs are rising, the IRR on new projects gets squeezed before the first machine is installed.","badge_label":"Capex Upcycle","badge_type":"b-exp"}
regime_classification.consumption: {"dimension":"consumption","metric_summary":"GST ₹231290 cr/mo; PV 32.1% YoY","signal_text":"GST at ₹2,31,290 cr / month is a record, but the honest read is that services-sector formalisation is doing as much work as genuine demand expansion — the 90th-percentile print reflects both. Passenger vehicle sales at 32.1% YoY and two-wheeler sales at 33.1% YoY are unambiguously strong, and commercial vehicle sales at 37.6% YoY confirm freight demand is real. The divergence to watch: credit card growth at 2.3% YoY — a 23rd-percentile reading — suggests the mass-market consumer is not leveraging up to fund this spending. That is either a sign of financial health or a sign that the top of the income distribution is carrying the entire consumption story.","badge_label":"Demand Surge","badge_type":"b-exp"}

signal_cards.1: {"signal_num":1,"signal_theme":"CREDIT CYCLE","status":"risk","title":"Deposit Gap Forces RBI's Hand","data_text":"Bank credit growth at 19.54% YoY (latest) vs deposit growth at 16.86% YoY — a 268 bps divergence widening for three consecutive months (13.8%→17.1%→19.4%→19.54% credit; 10.8%→17.8%→16.86% deposits). CD ratio at 82% credit-to-deposits, up from 81% last month, now at 75th percentile of 10-year range. NBFC credit growth decelerating to 15.4% YoY from 15.8%, signalling wholesale funding stress. Corporate bond issuance at ₹134,000 cr / month — firms are bypassing banks.","implication":"Overweight private banks with CASA ratios > 45% and retail deposit franchises (HDFC Bank, Kotak, Axis) — they will poach deposits from weaker peers. Underweight NBFCs with wholesale funding > 30% of liabilities (Bajaj Finance, Shriram Finance at risk). RBI will likely cut rates in Q2 FY27 to ease deposit pressure; position for 50-75 bps of cuts. Avoid small finance banks with CD ratios > 85%.","pct_10y":75,"pct_note":"CD ratio at 75th percentile historically preceded tighter liquidity and RBI rate cuts in 2019-20 and 2022-23. Current divergence is the widest since March 2023.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.2: {"signal_num":2,"signal_theme":"CAPEX TRIGGER","status":"positive","title":"Capex Upcycle Accelerating Into Q4","data_text":"IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (latest), up from 16.1% YoY prior month — third consecutive month of acceleration. Capacity utilisation at 77.4% of capacity (up from 75.6%), now at 68th percentile of 10-year range and above the 75% threshold that historically triggers fresh capex. Core sector growth at 4.8% YoY (down from 5.0%), but this masks strength in steel (+8.2%), cement (+6.1%), and power (+7.5%). Order books for capital equipment vendors are at 18-month highs.","implication":"Overweight capital goods manufacturers (Cummins, Kirloskar Electric, Bharat Heavy Electricals) and industrial conglomerates (Larsen & Toubro, Siemens). Increase exposure to cement (Ultratech, Ambuja) and steel (Tata Steel, JSW Steel) — capex-driven demand will sustain pricing power through Q4 FY27. Avoid consumer discretionary; capex is replacing consumption as the growth driver. Public sector capex execution remains strong; PSU stocks (NTPC, Power Grid) will benefit.","pct_10y":68,"pct_note":"Capacity utilisation at 77.4% is the highest since Q2 FY24 and historically precedes 12-18 months of sustained capex. Last time CU was this high (2021-22), capex growth averaged 18% YoY.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.3: {"signal_num":3,"signal_theme":"SIP / RETAIL FLOWS","status":"positive","title":"SIP Inflows Hit 94th Percentile Peak","data_text":"SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (latest), at 94th percentile of 10-year range — highest level on record. MF AUM at ₹83.39 lakh cr, up from ₹82.64 lakh cr, at 86th percentile. Equity MF net inflows at ₹32,994 cr / month (down from ₹38,307 cr prior month but still robust). SIP AUM at ₹17.68 lakh cr, at 91st percentile. However, SIP account growth has decelerated to 8.9% YoY (from 15% YoY six months ago) — average ticket size is rising, not account count.","implication":"Retail equity flows are structurally strong but increasingly concentrated among affluent investors. Overweight large-cap, dividend-paying stocks (HDFC Bank, TCS, Reliance) that appeal to SIP investors with rising disposable income. Avoid micro-cap and small-cap indices — SIP money is flowing to quality, not breadth. The 94th percentile SIP inflow level historically precedes 6-month market consolidation; take profits on momentum plays. Mutual fund houses with strong digital distribution (Axis MF, ICICI Prudential) will capture disproportionate share of flows.","pct_10y":94,"pct_note":"SIP inflows at 94th percentile have only been exceeded in 2021 (pre-correction) and 2024 (post-correction). Rising average ticket size signals late-cycle behaviour — affluent money entering, not mass retail.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.4: {"signal_num":4,"signal_theme":"OIL / COMMODITY RISK","status":"risk","title":"Fuel Inflation Spike Threatens Margin Compression","data_text":"Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (latest), up from 20.05% YoY prior month — at 95th percentile of 10-year range and the highest level since March 2023. WPI at 9.92% YoY, up from 9.78%, driven entirely by fuel and energy. Brent crude at $89.39 / bbl (down from $95.25 / bbl six months ago but volatile). Natural gas at $3.373 / MMBtu, up from $3.09 / MMBtu. India's oil import bill is running at $12-13 billion / month; at current prices, FY27 import bill will exceed $150 billion.","implication":"Reduce exposure to fuel-intensive sectors: airlines (IndiGo, SpiceJet), logistics (Allcargo, TCI Express), and fertilisers (Coromandel, UPL). Overweight energy stocks (ONGC, Reliance) and refiners (Indian Oil, Bharat Petroleum) — they benefit from higher crude and fuel spreads. Hedge INR weakness; oil imports will pressure CAD and rupee. RBI will struggle to cut rates if fuel inflation stays elevated; expect 25 bps cuts, not 50 bps. Avoid consumer staples with high logistics costs; margin compression will be severe.","pct_10y":95,"pct_note":"Fuel inflation at 95th percentile historically preceded 6-month periods of RBI rate pause and rupee depreciation (2022-23, 2018-19). Current spike is driven by geopolitical risk premium on Brent.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.5: {"signal_num":5,"signal_theme":"GLOBAL LIQUIDITY","status":"risk","title":"Fed Tightening Cycle Resumes; BOJ Shock Looms","data_text":"Fed funds rate at 3.88% p.a. (up from 3.75% p.a. prior month), rising for three consecutive months (3.63%→3.63%→3.75%→3.88%). US 10-year Treasury yield at 5.1% (down from 5.12% but at 93rd percentile of 10-year range). BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. (up from 1.0% p.a.), at 100th percentile — highest level since 2008. ECB deposit rate at 2.5% p.a., up from 2.25% p.a. US PMI Composite at 58.4 index (at 80th percentile), signalling persistent US growth. DXY at 103.869 index, rising for five consecutive months.","implication":"Reduce India equity exposure; carry trade unwind will pressure INR and FII flows. FII equity net flows at -₹4,516 cr / month (negative for two consecutive months). Overweight INR hedges and gold (though gold is falling, it will stabilise once Fed cuts). Expect 50-75 bps of RBI rate cuts in FY27 as Fed stays higher for longer — position for 10-year yield compression to 4.8-4.9%. Avoid high-beta, high-leverage plays; global liquidity is tightening. US equity valuations at 100th percentile (S&P 500 at 7,323.63 index) — expect 10-15% correction; this will trigger India selloff.","pct_10y":93,"pct_note":"US 10-year yield at 93rd percentile historically preceded 12-month periods of EM currency weakness and equity outflows (2022-23, 2018-19). BOJ at 100th percentile is unprecedented in this cycle — yen carry unwind will be violent.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.6: {"signal_num":6,"signal_theme":"INR / FX RESERVES","status":"watch","title":"Rupee Stability Masks Structural Pressure","data_text":"INR at 93.46 ₹ / USD (flat from 93.44 ₹ / USD), but oscillating between 93.46 and 94.34 ₹ / USD over past three months — RBI is actively defending the 94 level. FII equity net flows at -₹4,516 cr / month (negative). DXY at 103.869 index, rising for five consecutive months, putting structural pressure on INR. India's CAD is widening due to oil imports (₹150 billion / month) and gold imports (₹11,244 ₹ / g, at 94th percentile). Household debt at 47.8% of GDP (up from 45.5%), indicating domestic credit stress.","implication":"RBI will likely intervene to keep INR above 94.0 ₹ / USD, but reserves are finite. Overweight INR hedges (long USD calls, short INR forwards) for 6-month horizon. Avoid rupee-denominated debt; expect 50-75 bps of depreciation by Q2 FY27. Exporters (IT, pharma, textiles) will benefit from rupee weakness; overweight TCS, Infosys, Dr. Reddy's. Importers (oil, gold, electronics) will face margin pressure. RBI will likely cut rates faster than Fed to support INR; expect 75 bps of cuts by Q2 FY27.","pct_10y":87,"pct_note":"INR at 87th percentile weakness historically preceded 6-month periods of RBI rate cuts and rupee stabilisation (2022-23, 2018-19). Current DXY strength is the highest since 2023; structural pressure on INR will persist.","is_surprise":false}
signal_cards.7: {"signal_num":7,"signal_theme":"UNDER THE RADAR","status":"surprise","title":"Office Absorption Collapse Signals GCC Pivot","data_text":"Office absorption at 4.02 mn sq ft / quarter (latest), down 73% from 14.1 mn sq ft / quarter six months ago — at 0th percentile of 10-year range. Office vacancy at 13.4% (down from 14.5%), suggesting supply-side tightness, not demand strength. Yet Nifty IT is flat (TCS, Infosys, HCL Tech all trading at 2024 lows) despite office absorption collapse. Simultaneously, airline passenger traffic at 8.64 mn / month (at 0th percentile, down from 35.08 mn / month six months ago) — a data anomaly suggesting measurement error or structural shift. Retail mall vacancy at 11.15% (oscillating between 4.8% and 11.2%), indicating retail is bifurcating: premium malls thriving, secondary malls dying.","implication":"The office absorption collapse is NOT a demand crisis — it's a GCC (Global Capability Centre) pivot. Multinational tech firms are consolidating into fewer, larger campuses (Bangalore, Hyderabad, Pune) and exiting secondary markets (Mumbai, Delhi). This explains why Nifty IT is flat despite office weakness: traditional IT services are being displaced by GCCs and product engineering. Overweight GCC-beneficiary real estate (Embassy Office Parks, Mindspace REIT) and underweight traditional IT services. Expect 15-20% earnings downgrade for Tier-2 IT services (Mphasis, Persistent) as GCCs capture higher-margin work. Retail bifurcation means overweight premium malls (Inorbit, Oberoi) and underweight secondary retail REITs.","pct_10y":0,"pct_note":"Office absorption at 0th percentile is unprecedented in this dataset. The disconnect between office weakness and IT stock flatness suggests structural reallocation, not cyclical weakness. GCC consolidation is a 3-5 year trend that will reshape India's commercial real estate and IT services landscape.","is_surprise":true}

executive_summary.1:
{"para_num":1,"para_label":"India Macro Regime","para_html":"

Record GST, Negative Real Rates — Growth Is Real but Funded Expensively

The facts:

  • GST collections at ₹2,31,290 cr / month — 90th percentile of 10-year range — driven by services formalisation and vehicle demand, not a broad goods-economy surge.
  • PMI Composite at 56.5 and IIP capital goods at 16.9% YoY (third consecutive monthly acceleration) confirm expansion is not a statistical artefact.
  • But core sector growth slipped to 4.8% YoY from 5.0%, and headline CPI at 6.09% YoY has pushed the real repo rate negative — the RBI is inadvertently easing while inflation overshoots its own ceiling.
  • Household debt at 47.8% of GDP, up from 45.5%, signals the consumption boom has a leverage component that fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY will test.

The tension: The headline numbers — GDP 7.8% YoY, PMI 56.5, GST record — point to broad expansion; the plumbing — negative real rates, a widening credit-deposit gap, and fuel-driven margin compression — points to a cycle that is more fragile than the top line suggests.

Bottom line: Watch whether the RBI's November communiqué acknowledges the CPI overshoot; any language shift toward tightening bias reprices the entire rate-sensitive trade.

"}
executive_summary.2:
{"para_num":2,"para_label":"Global Macro Regime","para_html":"

US Re-Acceleration Meets BOJ Shock — EM Carry Trades in the Crossfire

The facts:

  • US GDP SAAR accelerated to 3.4% SAAR from 2.2%, and US PMI Composite at 58.4 (80th percentile) signals the Fed has no cover to pause further hikes.
  • Fed Funds at 3.88% p.a. — rising three months in a row — with US 10Y Treasury at 5.1% yield (93rd percentile); the bond market is doing additional tightening the Fed hasn't announced.
  • BOJ rate at 1.25% p.a. — 100th percentile, highest since 2008 — is the underappreciated tail: yen carry unwinds force EM asset liquidation with no warning.
  • But China PMI Composite at 49.5 (contraction) and Eurozone GDP at 0.4% YoY mean the global growth story is entirely a US story — and US growth at these rates is inflationary, not benign.

The tension: US re-acceleration keeps the Fed hawkish and the dollar bid; BOJ normalisation threatens the carry trade that has funded EM inflows for a decade. Both forces point the same direction for India: tighter external financial conditions.

Bottom line: DXY at 103.9 and rising for five consecutive months is the single most important external variable for INR and FII flows — watch the 105 level as the trigger for RBI intervention escalation.

"}
executive_summary.3:
{"para_num":3,"para_label":"Liquidity Conditions","para_html":"

SIP Autopilot Holds — But the Account Growth Engine Has Stalled

The facts:

  • SIP inflows at ₹32,160 cr / month (94th percentile) remain near record highs, but SIP account growth has decelerated to 8.9% YoY from 15% YoY six months ago — average ticket size is rising, not the participant base.
  • MF AUM at ₹83.39 lakh cr (86th percentile); equity MF net inflows at ₹32,994 cr net / month, down from ₹38,307 cr net / month — the marginal flow is decelerating.
  • FII equity net flows at -₹4,516 cr net / month; DII net at ₹6,222 cr net / month — domestic absorption is covering FII selling, but the DII cushion has shrunk from ₹58,502 cr net / month two months ago.
  • But corporate bond issuance at ₹1,34,000 cr / month signals firms are bypassing banks — a structural shift in credit intermediation that reduces bank fee income and deposit stickiness simultaneously.

The tension: Retail SIP flows are structurally robust, but the base of new participants is no longer expanding — the next leg of AUM growth requires either market appreciation or ticket-size inflation, both of which are fragile in a rising-rate, high-CPI environment.

Bottom line: SIP account growth below 10% YoY for two consecutive months would signal the retail participation story has peaked; watch the December SIP account print.

"}
executive_summary.4:
{"para_num":4,"para_label":"Equity + Real Estate Implications","para_html":"

Bank Nifty at 100th Percentile, REITs at Multi-Year Lows — Same Sector, Opposite Signals

The facts:

  • NRI buying is falling — NRI share of residential purchases at 18% (down 2 pp), though NRI share within premium/luxury holds at 32%; remittances at $155.1 bn (14.5% YoY) suggest capacity but not conviction.
  • Premium segment (₹80 lakh – ₹1.5 cr) is oversupplied by 3 pp (34% of launches vs 31% of sales); Hyderabad leads with sales up 15% YoY but 120% YoY launch surge risks a supply glut at 28 months unsold.
  • Bank Nifty at 62,039 (100th percentile) prices a banking system with pristine fundamentals; the CD ratio at 82% and NBFC stress say otherwise.
  • Embassy REIT at ₹370/unit, Mindspace at ₹345/unit, Brookfield at ₹263/unit — all down 12–31% from prior prints — while office absorption in Hyderabad surged 92% YoY to 4.2 mn sq ft / quarter.

The tension: Equities are pricing banking strength and real estate demand that the underlying data — CD ratio stress, NRI retreat, premium segment oversupply — does not support; REIT prices are pricing office collapse that city-level leasing data contradicts.

Bottom line: Avoid Bank Nifty at current valuations; selectively accumulate office REITs where city-level absorption (Hyderabad, Bengaluru) diverges from unit price declines.

"}
executive_summary.5:
{"para_num":5,"para_label":"Key Risks to Monitor","para_html":"

Three Fuses, One Detonator — Which Lights First

The facts:

  • Fuel inflation at 22.93% YoY (95th percentile) feeding into WPI at 9.92% YoY — if Brent recovers toward $95/bbl from $89.39/bbl, the FY27 import bill exceeds $150 bn and CAD widens beyond RBI's comfort zone.
  • BOJ at 1.25% p.a. (100th percentile, highest since 2008) — a further 25 bps hike triggers yen carry unwind, FII selling accelerates beyond -₹4,516 cr net / month, and INR tests the 94.34 RBI defence line.
  • CD ratio at 82% (75th percentile) with credit at 19.54% YoY — if deposit growth slips below 15% YoY, the RBI issues risk-weight circulars on unsecured lending within one quarter, repricing NBFC and small-bank credit.
  • US CPI at 3.72% YoY rising three months in a row with Core PCE at 3.12% YoY — a hot November print forces a Fed hike, pushes US 10Y above 5.25% yield, and triggers simultaneous EM outflows.

The tension: Each risk is individually manageable; the danger is sequencing — a BOJ shock triggers FII outflows, INR depreciation amplifies fuel inflation, and the RBI is forced to hike into a slowing credit cycle.

Bottom line: Watch US Core PCE for November (due this week): a print above 3.3% YoY makes a December Fed hike near-certain and is the single most important data point for India's external liquidity this month.

"}
